gotchas: The MT75 is not a device Cabin Hub can poll. It is a display that acts as a Modbus MASTER on the bus — the same collision docs/DEVICES.md already records for the MT50. Its own manual confirms the role: "Check whether the solar controller's ID is 1; if not, set it to 1. Check whether the ID of the inverter is 3; if not,

One master per RS-485 segment. A gateway and an MT75 on the same wire will collide; tolerate the retries or unplug the meter. The MT75 has two RJ45 RS-485 ports and is designed to poll a controller on one and an inverter on the other — the vendor's own topology assumes it is the only master.

Its slave-ID expectations are a free confirmation of cabin-epever's defaults: controller = 1, inverter = 3, which is exactly what xtra.rs and ipower.rs ship and why the two EPEver devices at this site coexist on one bus untouched.

The MT75 takes its 5 VDC from the connected controller or inverter over the RJ45 — pins 1 and 2, the same pins that must never be carried through to a third device. Self-consumption 14 mA at 5 V without backlight, 26 mA with, 100 mA peak with backlight and dry contact.

Vendor compatibility list, verbatim from the MT75 manual §10: controllers — XTRA-N series, TRIRON series, Tracer-AN series, Tracer-BN series (cables shipped with the MT75); iTracer-AD / iTracer-ND series (cables sold separately). Inverters — IPower series (1 kW or above), IPower-Plus series, NPower series, SHI series.
